CL000001.comment:
An IFSC (Indian Financial System Code) is an 11-digit alphanumeric code used for electronic funds transfers (NEFT, RTGS, IMPS) in India. It consists of the first four letters (bank name), a fifth character (0), and the last six characters (branch code)

Example: SBIN0000123 (State Bank of India [SBIN], Branch 000123).

Common IFSC Examples:
State Bank of India (SBI): SBIN0000123
HDFC Bank: HDFC0000509
Axis Bank: UTIB0000124
Kotak Mahindra Bank: KKBK0000172
Citibank: CITI0000003

Key Components Breakdown:
First 4 letters: Represent the bank (e.g., HDFC, SBIN, ICIC).
5th character: Always zero (0), reserved for future use.
Last 6 digits: Represent the specific branch code.
